title: Finite-energy lattice percolation with internal critical probability one
description:
For every integer d at least 2, we construct a nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the integer lattice Z^d whose law is invariant under every graph automorphism and mixing under translations. It has ordinary finite energy: both single-edge conditional states have strictly positive probability given all the other output edges. Almost surely there is a unique infinite component C, but the quenched internal Bernoulli bond and site critical probabilities of X and C equal one. Every independent thinning with retention p below one destroys all infinite components. This gives an affirmative construction for the historical ordinary-energy question of Benjamini, Haggstrom and Schramm, restated in Benjamini's Saint-Flour notes and by Benjamini and Tassion.

The construction develops Haggstrom-Mester's published one-ended-tree summable-flip mechanism. Tree edges are deleted with probability 2^(-s), where s is their finite-side size; a non-tree edge is inserted with probability 2^(-M), where M is the maximum finite-side size along its connecting tree path. This dimension independent rule suppresses every bypass and leaves eventually singleton cut boundaries along each ray. Timar's established equivariant one-ended spanning-tree theorem supplies the all-dimensional input. The note also proves a planar bounded-cutset consequence of the exact fixed-phase midpoint projection of the older Haggstrom-Mester site model, whose unchanged flip rates are 4^(-s). That consequence is a deduction supplied here, not a theorem located in the inspected older paper. No wholly new planar perturbation mechanism, verified first resolution, certified novelty of the all-dimensional rule, or worldwide current-open-status claim is made. No uniform energy bound or failure of every uniform marginal bound is asserted.

The deposit contains a five-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all 27 frozen original files and three evidence archives with 15 members, six independent analytical or priority audit families, primary-source/version/hash locators, an external-pin inventory verifier and a deterministic rebuild tool. The automated checks reproduce source and archive identities with 11 parser/path rejection controls in normal and optimized modes; they do not certify the infinite mathematical proof or historical priority. Downloaded publications, source extracts, renders, and raw input corpora are excluded. OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, proof development, drafting, coding, and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed.
